All of South Korea’s military forces will be trained as drone operators in a sweeping overhaul of its warfare strategy, the defence minister has said.

“All soldiers should be able to use drones like a second personal firearm,” Ahn Gyu-back, who heads the defence ministry in Seoul, said on Friday.

rfi.title: Israel's targeting of Gaza's children proves genocidal intent, UN inquiry finds
rfi.description: The deliberate targeting of Palestinian children is central to a United Nations-mandated report's conclusion that Israel is committing genocide in Gaza. The commission argues that children have not only been victims of the war, but have been targeted in ways that help establish genocidal intent. Israel has dismissed the findings of the report, released this week, as "defamatory".

rfi.title: France heatwave overwhelms hospitals and forces Pride march delay
rfi.description: Emergency doctors at one of Paris's biggest hospitals warned on Friday that wards had become dangerously overcrowded after a week of soaring temperatures, as authorities restricted public alcohol consumption, organisers postponed the annual Pride march and €130 million was pledged to help schools adapt to climate change.

rfi.title: Current Europe heatwave 'impossible' without human-induced climate change
rfi.description: A study comparing the heatwave that has swept across Europe this week with heatwaves in 1976 and 2003 has found that human-caused climate change is "unequivocally" responsible for the extreme heat over the last week – with France recording its hottest day since records began in 1947 on Wednesday.

rfi.title: Calls for child protection reforms in wake of schoolgirl Lyhanna's death
rfi.description: An investigation into previous child rape allegations against the suspect in the death of a schoolgirl in southern France has revealed failures by prosecutors and police. The case has unleashed a wave of criticism over how sexual and gender-based violence cases are handled in France, with victims, families and advocates pushing for reform.

rfi.title: Historic heatwave catches Europe's fashion industry unprepared
rfi.description: The most coveted accessory at the Paris Fashion Week shows this week was not a bag, a sneaker or a watch. It was an ice pack.

rfi.title: Paris court gives oil giant TotalEnergies deadline to tighten climate policies
rfi.description: A court in Paris ruled on Thursday that energy giant TotalEnergies must account for its consumers’ greenhouse gas emissions, giving the French company six months to adjust a legally mandated risk assessment.

rfi.title: France told to do more to protect children from human trafficking
rfi.description: France must step up efforts to prevent human trafficking and improve support for victims, particularly children and young people, the Council of Europe has said, warning that weaknesses in the country's child protection system continue to leave minors exposed to exploitation.

rfi.title: Pépé stars as Cote d'Ivoire beat Curaçao to reach knockout stages for first time
rfi.description: Nicolas Pépé scored twice on Thursday to fire Cote d'Ivoire to the second phase of a World Cup tournament for the first time with a 2-0 win over Curaçao.

rfi.title: Relief in sight as temperatures set to fall in France after record heatwave
rfi.description: Temperatures are expected to fall in France from Thursday evening after another day of extreme heat that put 72 of mainland France's 96 departments on red alert, affecting more than 50 million people.

rfi.title: South African anti-migrant groups defend planned ‘Liberation March’
rfi.description: A coalition of South African organisations campaigning against undocumented migrants has defended its plans for nationwide demonstrations on 30 June, insisting the marches will be peaceful despite rising tensions and recent deadly unrest.

rfi.title: Kenya mounts huge security operation on Gen Z protest anniversary
rfi.description: Kenyan police put on a massive show of force Thursday in a bid to prevent protests marking two years since a landmark Gen Z uprising.

rfi.title: Macron to host Meloni in Antibes as France and Italy seek closer ties
rfi.description: French President Emmanuel Macron will host Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni in the French seaside resort of Antibes, as the two leaders try to revive a relationship that has been marked by political differences.

rfi.title: Zelensky to miss Poland summit as Second World War row escalates
rfi.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky will not attend a major conference on rebuilding Ukraine being held in Poland this week, as a dispute between the two countries over Second World War remembrance threatens to overshadow talks.

rfi.title: South Africa beat South Korea to reach World Cup knockout stages for first time
rfi.description: Thapelo Maseko scored mid way through the second half against South Korea to take South Africa into the knockout stages at a World Cup for the first time.

rfi.title: Digital euro wins key EU backing as lawmakers approve draft rules
rfi.description: The European Union has moved a step closer to creating a digital euro, after members of the European Parliament passed a crucial vote on the virtual currency.

rfi.title: Brazil overpower Scotland to take Group C as Morocco wear down Haiti
rfi.description: Brazil outclassed Scotland 3-0 on Wednesday night in Miami to claim Group C at the 2026 World Cup. Carlo Ancelotti's men started the final round of games in pole position following their 3-0 win over Haiti on 19 June while Morocco edged past Scotland 1-0.

rfi.title: France announces first Ebola case in doctor returned from DR Congo
rfi.description: French health authorities on Wednesday announced the first confirmed case of Ebola identified on national territory – a doctor who had returned from the Democratic Republic of Congo.

rfi.title: US releases experimental Ebola drug for DR Congo outbreak trials
rfi.description: Experimental Ebola drugs are being shipped to Democratic Republic of Congo as the United States releases doses of a treatment for clinical trials in a widening outbreak that has caused more than 1,000 cases and over 250 deaths, the World Health Organization and US officials have said.

euronews.title: EU countries move to revive temporary message-scanning regime, but it could backfire
euronews.description: The proposed detection regime for child sexual abuse material was rejected by the European Parliament in March, and reviving it could derail talks on a longer-term law.

euronews.title: Heatwave in France: baby dies in A&E, fourth child death this week
euronews.description: An 18-month-old baby died after being found unconscious with heatstroke in a car in Marseille on Tuesday 23 June. A parent is believed to have left the child on the La Timone medical campus car park while going to work.

euronews.title: Home Heroes and Japanese Stars Shine in Qingdao
euronews.description: The Qingdao Grand Prix opened with memorable performances as home favourite Wenna Zhuang delighted the local fans. Hayato Kondo claimed a second Qingdao title, Kokoro Fujishiro earned her first Grand Prix gold, Hifumi Abe added another title, Maysa Pardayeva celebrated a maiden World Tour victory.

euronews.title: EU energy ministers secure greater role in bloc's future power grid after rows with Brussels
euronews.description: The EU's Cypriot Presidency has successfully reached an agreement among EU countries that paves the way for talks between the European Parliament and the Council.

euronews.title: France heatwave: homeless people on the front line against the heat
euronews.description: With 61 departments still on red heatwave alert, people sleeping rough are among the most exposed. In Marseille, outreach teams step up to provide water, support and shelter.

euronews.title: Kyiv mayor at Ukraine Recovery Conference in Gdańsk: 'Ukraine must do exactly what Poland did'
euronews.description: Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko told the Ukraine Recovery Conference in Gdańsk that, despite recent diplomatic tensions between the two countries, the atmosphere at the gathering was friendly, and that Ukraine should look to Poland as a model for infrastructure development and modernisation.

euronews.title: Why extreme heat makes people angrier and how our brain reacts to heatwaves
euronews.description: Extreme heat not only harms the body but can also trigger a cascade of mental health effects ranging from irritability and anxiety to increased aggression.

euronews.title: Russia and Ukraine swap 160 soldiers each in latest prisoner exchange
euronews.description: The United Arab Emirates brokered the handover, which brought home fighters captured in the early weeks of the full-scale invasion.

euronews.title: Ukraine: Zaporizhzhia ablaze after Russian missile and drone attack leaves at least nine hurt
euronews.description: Russian missile and drone strikes set an office building ablaze in central Zaporizhzhia on 26 June, injuring at least nine people and triggering a major emergency response.

euronews.title: Panting and hyperthermia: Paris vet sees uptick in pets being admitted due to extreme heat
euronews.description: Several days of extreme heat across France are sending large numbers of pets to the vet.

euronews.title: To use air con or not? The facts behind the politicised battle to stay cool in Europe
euronews.description: French politicians have drawn ideological battle lines over air conditioning as Europe struggles with record-breaking temperatures. What do experts say about the debate?

euronews.title: Von der Leyen to visit Azerbaijan and Armenia to build on EU engagement
euronews.description: The European Commission president will visit Baku and Yerevan to build on the EU’s strategic engagement with the South Caucasus and to strengthen energy cooperation, trade and regional connectivity for the EU economies.

euronews.title: Watch: South Korea holds first live-fire drill against drone swarms
euronews.description: South Korea's air force carried out its first live-fire exercise against a simulated swarm drone attack. Military forces used Vulcan air-defense guns, a portable laser and shotguns to intercept all 50 drones during the drill.

euronews.title: Barcelona proposes to nearly triple tourist tax on cruise ship passengers to €30 a day
euronews.description: The hiked fee would only apply to cruises that make port calls and spend less than 12 hours docked.

euronews.title: Can travel solve the loneliness epidemic? WeRoad's co-founder Fabio Bin thinks so
euronews.description: Speaking to Euronews in Cannes after being shortlisted for the European CMO of the Year Award, Fabio Bin explained he turned a personal frustration into a fast-growing social travel brand.

euronews.title: Tashkent International Investment Forum ends with €37.6bn in deals
euronews.description: More than 10,000 participants, including delegates from 102 countries, examined market access, transport links, green power, digital exports and the policies needed to turn commitments into operating projects.

euronews.title: Buurtzorg: the Dutch proximity health care revolution
euronews.description: In the Netherlands, Buurtzorg’s self-managed nurses provide holistic home care and social support, helping older people live independently with dignity.

euronews.title: 'Marketing is more important than ever': Serviceplan CEO at European CMO of the Year awards
euronews.description: Speaking to Euronews, Serviceplan Group CEO Florian Haller said marketing has evolved far beyond traditional advertising, and now sits at the centre of the "whole customer journey" where "data, technology and creativity" meet.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, canicule : le plan blanc déclenché dans tous les hôpitaux d’Ile-de-France, en raison d’un système de soins « sous tension »
lemonde.description: Les SAMU rapportent notamment une activité en forte hausse (61 % d’appels supplémentaires par rapport à la semaine dernière, 75 % en plus par rapport à la même époque l’année dernière), principalement pour des malaises.

lemonde.title: Séismes au Venezuela : le bilan s’alourdit à 589 morts et près de 3 000 blessés
lemonde.description: Les recherches se poursuivent dans les décombres d’immeubles qui se sont effondrés pour tenter de secourir des personnes prises au piège, au lendemain d’un double séisme extrêmement puissant.

lemonde.title: En Ukraine, en temps de guerre, ceux qui partent, ceux qui restent : la vie suspendue à Sloviansk et Kramatorsk
lemonde.description: « Donbass, la guerre jusqu’à l’usure » (2/2). Dans cette région industrielle occupée à 80 % par les troupes russes, les villes de Sloviansk et de Kramatorsk sont devenues le cœur du dispositif défensif ukrainien. Une partie de leurs habitants choisissent de fuir vers des zones plus sûres. Les autres tentent de survivre comme ils le peuvent.

lemonde.title: France-Norvège : Erling Haaland et ses coéquipiers, purs produits de la fabrique à champions d’un pays qui mise sur le sport
lemonde.description: En Norvège, dont l’équipe nationale affronte la France, vendredi, en phase de groupes de la Coupe du monde 2026, le sport fait partie de l’identité nationale. Le pays ne cesse de sortir des champions, dans de nombreuses disciplines. Les acteurs de cette réussite ont livré au « Monde » les secrets de leur méthode.

lemonde.title: A Vaca Muerta, en Patagonie, l’eldorado du pétrole argentin attire des milliers de travailleurs rêvant d’une vie meilleure
lemonde.description: Cette vaste formation géologique battue par les vents, en Patagonie argentine, enregistre des niveaux de production de pétrole record. Le pays de Javier Milei mise fortement sur l’exportation d’hydrocarbures pour tirer sa croissance, sans se préoccuper de la question environnementale.

lemonde.title: Un apéro avec Bigflo & Oli : « Pendant longtemps, on nous a surnommés “les cafards du rap français” »
lemonde.description: Chaque semaine, « L’Epoque » paie son coup. Avant d’enchaîner les dates de concerts dans les festivals de l’été, les frères rappeurs, qui se sont débarrassés d’une image un peu lisse, se confient sur la longévité de leur duo.

lemonde.title: En Nouvelle-Calédonie, une élection cruciale après une campagne sans enthousiasme
lemonde.description: Deux ans après les violences qui ont secoué l’archipel, les Néo-Calédoniens désigneront, dimanche 28 juin, les membres des trois assemblées de province et du congrès. Un scrutin majeur, mais qui ne suscite pas d’engouement.

lemonde.title: Volkswagen pourrait supprimer 100 000 emplois dans le monde
lemonde.description: Le géant automobile allemand, qui emploie 657 000 salariés, est confronté à une chute de ses ventes en Chine, autrefois son premier marché, et alors que les exportateurs chinois lui imposent une redoutable concurrence, notamment sur l’électrique.

lemonde.title: L’épidémie d’Ebola en RDC a fait 304 morts, selon le dernier bilan des autorités
lemonde.description: Le virus a contaminé 1 115 personnes en République démocratique du Congo depuis le 15 mai, selon les chiffres de l’Institut national de santé publique.

lemonde.title: « L’influence de la mécène Aline Foriel-Destezet sur la musique classique et l’opéra en dit long sur les bouleversements de la culture »
lemonde.description: En inaugurant, mardi, une nouvelle salle consacrée à la musique classique à Evian, Aline Foriel-Destezet montre une nouvelle fois son influence dans un secteur en mal de soutien public et où l’argent est de plus en plus dirigé vers les structures privées, relève Michel Guerrin, rédacteur en chef au « Monde », dans sa chronique.

lemonde.title: Safran veut racheter le fabricant français de drones sous-marins Exail
lemonde.description: L’industriel de l’aéronautique et de la défense a fait une offre pour racheter l’entreprise à la famille Gorgé pour plus de 2,2 milliards d’euros.

lemonde.title: A Pékin, un petit avion s’écrase dans le plus haut gratte-ciel de la ville
lemonde.description: La cause de l’incident n’est pas claire et les autorités n’ont pas publié de communiqué à ce sujet.

lemonde.title: Centrale biomasse de Gardanne : la poursuite de l’exploitation accordée
lemonde.description: Forcée par le Conseil d’Etat en 2023 à prendre en compte les effets indirects de son activité, en particulier sur les forêts locales, l’entreprise avait dû revoir son plan d’approvisionnement et lancer une vaste enquête publique sur l’impact environnemental de l’approvisionnement en bois de sa centrale.

lemonde.title: « Opération Dragon. La révolution Bruce Lee », sur Arte.tv : comment le surdoué du kung-fu est devenu le bras vengeur des opprimés
lemonde.description: Ce documentaire jubilatoire retrace le parcours de ce Hongkongais qui, en quatre films, a conquis la planète et réinventé un genre cinématographique où la liberté est au bout du nunchaku.

lemonde.title: Malakoff Humanis, poids lourd de la complémentaire santé et de la prévoyance, visé par une enquête pour corruption
lemonde.description: Une somme de 7 millions d’euros pourrait correspondre aux commissions perçues pour un rôle d’intermédiaire par Thomas Vendôme Investment, qui se présente comme une « société indépendante spécialisée dans la levée de fonds et le conseil stratégique en entreprise ». Le groupe récuse « fermement l’existence de toute rétrocommission ».

lemonde.title: A l’ère de l’IA, les universités chinoises bouleversent leurs cursus
lemonde.description: Une refonte universitaire est en cours à travers le pays pour coller aux priorités économiques du gouvernement chinois et tenter de résorber le chômage des jeunes. Pour se maintenir, certaines spécialités comme les langues vivantes doivent s’adosser aux sciences dures.

france24fr.title: Canicule en France : les hôpitaux parisiens "saturés"
france24fr.description: De premiers décès probablement liés à la chaleur, les hôpitaux parisiens "saturés": restée confrontée jeudi à une canicule "totalement inédite", la France s'inquiète de ses conséquences sanitaires, malgré une première rétrogradation de départements en vigilance orange dans la soirée.

france24fr.title: La Cour suprême américaine lève une protection juridique contre l'expulsion de 350 000 Haïtiens
france24fr.description: La Cour suprême américaine majoritairement conservatrice a accordé jeudi un succès à l'administration Trump dans sa politique d'expulsions massives d'immigrés en l'autorisant à révoquer un statut protégeant 350 000 Haïtiens et 6 000 Syriens.

france24fr.title: Mathieu Forget, l'homme qui défie la gravité
france24fr.description: Danseur, photographe, directeur artistique…Mathieu Forget a fait de la lévitation sa signature. Surnommé "the flying man", ou "l'homme volant" il célèbre dix ans de carrière avec "Lévitation", un livre qui rassemble ses photographies spectaculaires réalisées aux quatre coins du monde.

france24fr.title: Voyageur atteint d'Ebola : Air France a interrompu ses vols Paris-Kinshasa, reprise samedi
france24fr.description: Air France a suspendu ses vols entre Paris et Kinshasa à la suite de l'identification d'un cas positif au virus Ebola ayant voyagé sur cette ligne mardi, a indiqué vendredi la compagnie à l'AFP. L'épidémie de maladie Ebola en République démocratique du Congo a fait 304 morts, selon un dernier bilan des autorités sanitaires congolaises.

france24fr.title: La Crimée placée en "situation d'urgence" après les attaques ukrainiennes
france24fr.description: La Crimée annexée a été placée en "situation d'urgence" au niveau régional, ont annoncé vendredi les responsables russes locaux, un régime visant à faire face aux conséquences des récentes frappes ukrainiennes ayant causé de graves pénuries de carburant et d'électricité.

france24fr.title: Séisme au Venezuela : les recherches pour retrouver des survivants s'intensifient
france24fr.description: Les recherches pour retrouver des survivants s'intensifient vendredi au Venezuela, où l'aide internationale commence à arriver, presque deux jours après deux séismes dévastateurs dont le bilan a plus que doublé pour atteindre 589 morts.

france24fr.title: Le Paris des Arts à Fès, au Maroc!
france24fr.description: Cette semaine, le Paris des Arts pose ses caméras à Fès, cité impériale marocaine, à l’occasion de la 29ème édition du Festival des musiques sacrées du monde, qui met à l’honneur le dialogue des cultures et des spiritualités.

france24fr.title: Pourquoi le dôme de chaleur est un phénomène météo et pas une “attaque” climatique contre la France
france24fr.description: La canicule actuelle aurait été provoquée par une manipulation du climat : un dôme de chaleur aurait été créé artificiellement au-dessus de la France. C’est ce que prétendent des internautes qui estiment que l’Hexagone ferait l’objet d’une “attaque” climatique. Un dôme de chaleur n'est en fait qu'un phénomène météo amplifié par le réchauffement climatique expliquent les experts.

france24fr.title: Canicule en France : les écoles face à l'urgence de la rénovation
france24fr.description: Plus de 130 millions d'euros pour financer en urgence des systèmes de rafraîchissement et des travaux dans les écoles, particulièrement touchées par la canicule, ont été annoncés vendredi par EDF, la Banque des territoires, la Banque postale et le gouvernement. D'autres établissements s'adaptent aux conditions climatiques. Les précisions de Damien Coursodon, proviseur du lycée E. Herriot et membre du syndicat ID-FO.

france24fr.title: Canicule : à Paris, le festival Solidays annulé, la Marche des Fiertés reportée
france24fr.description: Le festival Solidays a été annulé et la Marche des Fiertés reportée, vendredi, à la demande du préfet de police de Paris qui menaçait de les interdire en invoquant la persistance d'une canicule mettant à rude épreuve les secours et les hôpitaux.

france24fr.title: De nombreux événements festifs et sportifs annulés en France
france24fr.description: L'épisode caniculaire qui sévit en France chamboule les événements du week-end. Depuis plusieurs jours, de nombreuses compétitions amateurs sont annulées un peu partout dans l'hexagone en raison de ces chaleurs extrêmes, ainsi que plusieurs concerts et festivals.

france24fr.title: Guerre au Moyen-Orient : Siavosh Ghazi, témoin du conflit depuis Téhéran
france24fr.description: L'Agence internationale de l'énergie atomique (AIEA) estime qu'un dispositif de vérification "très poussé" est désormais nécessaire en Iran pour garantir l'absence de programme nucléaire militaire. Derrière cet enjeu diplomatique se cachent des vies bouleversées par la guerre. Siavosh Ghazi, correspondant de RFI et France 24 en Iran, en témoigne dans Carnet de guerre, récit de quarante jours dans Téhéran sous les bombardements.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : qualification historique pour la Côte d'Ivoire
france24fr.description: La Côte d'Ivoire a validé son billet pour la phase à élimination directe de la Coupe du monde, pour la première fois de son histoire. Victoire 2 buts à 0 contre le petit poucet Curaçao. Dans le même temps, l'Équateur a créé la surprise en l'emportant face à l'Allemagne pour aller chercher une qualification qui semblait inespérée après ses deux premiers matchs.

france24fr.title: 🔴 Séismes au Venezuela : le bilan monte à 589 morts, annonce la présidente par intérim
Espagne : travailler sans arrêt pour lutter contre la chaleur
france24fr.description: Pour faire face aux fortes chaleurs, de nombreux Espagnols adoptent les "journées intensives" : ils concentrent leur temps de travail... pour terminer à 15 heures. Notre correspondante Maude Petit-Jové nous explique

france24fr.title: L’Agence internationale de l'énergie atomique veut un contrôle "très poussé" du nucléaire iranien
france24fr.description: L’AIEA appelle vendredi à un dispositif de vérification "très poussé" en Iran, après la guerre. Malgré un accord censé empêcher le développement d’armes nucléaires, l’accès aux sites reste limité et le sort des stocks d’uranium demeure flou, au cœur de négociations tendues avec Washington.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : Pourquoi la France est le plus grand vivier de joueurs du tournoi ?
france24fr.description: Sur les 1 248 joueurs qui participent au Mondial, 99 sont nés et ont été formés en France, un record. Certaines sélections comme l’Algérie, le Maroc, Haïti et le Sénégal comptent au moins un tiers de leur effectif formé dans l’Hexagone. Des chiffres qui ne doivent rien au hasard et qui témoignent notamment d’un savoir-faire à la française quand il s’agit de former les joueurs. Notre journaliste Thimoté Bozzetto vous explique.

france24fr.title: Calais : rencontre avec des migrants qui tentent la traversée de la Manche en bateau
france24fr.description: La Manche est devenue l'une des routes migratoires les plus empruntées d'Europe. Chaque année, des milliers de migrants tentent de rejoindre clandestinement le Royaume-Uni à bord d'embarcations de fortune. Malgré le renforcement des moyens de surveillance et de coopération entre Londres et Paris, plusieurs milliers de personnes parviennent encore à effectuer cette traversée périlleuse. Nos reporters Pauline Godart, Claire Paccalin et Mohamed Farhat ont réussi à rencontrer des migrants sur la pla

zeit.title: Künstlerische Fächer in der Oberstufe: Ist das Kunst, oder kann das weg?
zeit.description: Bald gibt es in Hamburg weniger Kunst- und Musikunterricht, fürchtet die Kulturszene. Die Schulbehörde dementiert: Die Fächer bleiben Pflicht – mit einer Einschränkung.

zeit.title: Fußball-WM 2026: Bastian Schweinsteiger wehrt sich gegen Rassismus-Vorwürfe
zeit.description: Nach Äußerungen in der ARD über »afrikanischen Fußball« wird Schweinsteiger Rassismus vorgeworfen. Er wehrt sich. Uruguays Team meutert gegen den Trainer. Das Liveblog

zeit.title: Feuerwehr im Einsatz: Leiche nach Flächenbrand in Rottenburg entdeckt
Triathlon: Hitze: Ironman Frankfurt wird verkürzt
Wetter: Hitzewarnung für MV: Bis zu 39 Grad am Wochenende erwartet
Wassertemperatur: Rhein hat 28 Grad erreicht - Fischsterben in Mosel droht
Mecklenburg-Vorpommern: Großbrand bei Neustrelitz - Stromleitung abgeschaltet
Alkoholverbot: »Wenn schon trinken, dann im Schatten«
zeit.description: Paris verhängt ein Alkoholverbot, weil Alkohol bei Hitze besonders schadet. Gesundheitsforscher Hajo Zeeb erklärt, was dann im Körper passiert und worauf man achten muss.

zeit.title: Stellenabbau bei Volkswagen : Der Tabubruch
zeit.description: Volkswagen will noch mehr sparen als bekannt, 100.000 Jobs könnten wegfallen. Kritiker fürchten jetzt, der Vorstand könnte das mit einem Trick durchsetzen.

zeit.title: Einsatz: Fahrzeug brennt aus - Person tot geborgen
Suche geht weiter: Leichen von zwei Männern nach Sprung in Bodensee entdeckt
Feuerwehr-Einsatz: Jugendlicher fällt von Boot – Badesee für Suche gesperrt
Geheiminformationen: Trump-Kritiker John Bolton bekennt sich vor Gericht schuldig
zeit.description: Trumps Sicherheitsberater hat vor Gericht zugegeben, geheime Informationen zurückgehalten zu haben. Er einigte sich mit der Staatsanwaltschaft auf eine hohe Geldbuße.

zeit.title: Hochzeit von Taylor Swift: Heiraten gegen den Weltuntergang
zeit.description: Taylor Swift hält Hochzeit – hochöffentlich und hochgeheim. Es wird die wichtigste prominente Vermählung seit der von Lady Diana. Und sie bedeutet mehr als Unterhaltung.

zeit.title: Hitzewelle: Höchsttemperatur in Juni in Deutschland mit über 40 Grad gemessen
zeit.description: In Saarbrücken ist eine neue Höchsttemperatur von über 40 Grad gemessen worden. Der Großbrand in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern nähert sich einer ICE-Strecke. Das Liveblog

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Hunderttausend Stellen werden gestrichen: Die Krise bei VW ist ein Menetekel für den Standort Deutschland
nzz.description: Jahrelang haben die EU und die Bundesregierung eine Politik gegen die Autoindustrie betrieben. Jetzt droht der Branche der Niedergang –  und Deutschland der Verlust von Wohlstand. Das Land braucht eine 180-Grad-Wende in der Wirtschafts- und Energiepolitik.

nzz.title: Präsidentenanwärter und Leopardenretter: Putins langjähriger Weggefährte Sergei Iwanow ist gestorben
nzz.description: Der einstige KGB-Agent im Westen war mehr als zwei Jahrzehnte lang ein prägendes Gesicht im Umfeld des Kremlchefs. Am Schluss fand er als Naturschützer seine eigentliche Berufung.

nzz.title: Volkswagen könnte bis zu 100 000 Stellen abbauen und vier Werke schliessen
nzz.description: Ein Konzept der Konzernführung sieht beispiellose Einschnitte vor: In der Folge würde sich der deutsche Autobauer aus weiten Teilen Deutschlands verabschieden. Der Widerstand ist gross.

nzz.title: Das jüngste Opfer von Hegseths Säuberungswelle: Der Befehlshaber der US-Armee in Europa räumt seinen Posten
nzz.description: Chris Donahue sei «wie ein Actionheld aus einem Comic», sagte einst der Nato-Oberbefehlshaber. Er verliess als letzter amerikanischer Soldat Afghanistan – und wird nun auch aus Europa abgezogen.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Schwere Erdbeben erschüttern Venezuela: Zahl der Todesopfer steigt auf 589 +++ Staatsfernsehen zeigt Ankunft von Rettungskräften aus der Schweiz und Deutschland
nzz.description: Innerhalb weniger Minuten richteten zwei Erdbeben in Venezuela verheerende Schäden an. Rettungskräfte suchen unter den Trümmern nach Überlebenden. Über das Ausmass der Schäden ist wenig bekannt.

nzz.title: KURZMELDUNGEN - Schweiz: Feuerwerksinitiative kommt zur Abstimmung
Die Genfer Regierung hat ihre Ziele für den G-7-Gipfel erreicht. Doch ein Polizeieinsatz sorgt für Kritik
nzz.description: Der Staatsrat zieht eine positive Bilanz seines Sicherheitsdispositivs während des G-7-Gipfels im französischen Évian-les-Bains. Es bleiben jedoch Fragen offen.

nzz.title: Grossanlässe trotz Hitze: So funktioniert ein Triathlon bei 36 Grad
nzz.description: Für das Wochenende werden rekordverdächtig hohe Temperaturen vorausgesagt. Trotzdem finden in Zürich grosse Sportanlässe statt. Die Spitäler treffen Vorkehrungen.

nzz.title: Wer fährt an den Nato-Gipfel? In Tschechien tragen Staatspräsident Pavel und Regierungschef Babis einen Machtkampf um die Aussenpolitik aus
nzz.description: Die Regierung Babis wollte verhindern, dass der Staatspräsident Pavel nach Ankara reist. Dieser vermutet einen Racheakt – und erwirkte beim Verfassungsgericht seine Teilnahme am Nato-Gipfel.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Hitze in Europa: AKW Beznau wegen hoher Temperatur der Aare abgestellt +++ Pride-Parade in Paris abgesagt
nzz.description: Wo ist es gerade besonders heiss? Und was sind die Auswirkungen auf Mensch und Umwelt? Hier finden Sie die neuesten Meldungen zu Hitzerekorden, Dürren und Bränden in Europa.

nzz.title: Grosse Überwachung von kleinen Insekten: wie sich das Tessin gegen die Tigermücke wehrt
nzz.description: Invasive Insekten wie die Tigermücke breiten sich aus. Mit einem neuen Überwachungsprogramm rüsten sich Bund und Kantone gegen die Einschleppung tropischer Erreger.

nzz.title: An der WM rudern die Norweger und präsentieren sich als Wikinger – doch dieses Bild provoziert
nzz.description: Norwegen spielt erstmals seit 1998 an einer WM und zieht in den Sechzehntelfinal ein. Bei Toren der Nationalmannschaft schlagen bisweilen sogar Seismometer aus.

nzz.title: DATENANALYSE - Live-Daten zeigen: In Basel wurde der Hitzerekord von 2003 geknackt, in Zürich steht man kurz davor
nzz.description: Hitzetage und Tropennächte sind deutlich häufiger geworden. Dieser Trend wird sich fortsetzen. Besonders in den Städten kühlt die Luft kaum mehr ab. Die neusten Zahlen zur Hitze in der grafischen Übersicht.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Krieg in der Ukraine: Ausnahmezustand auf der Halbinsel Krim verhängt +++ Russland meldet heftige ukrainische Drohnenangriffe
nzz.description: Seit über vier Jahren führt Russland Krieg gegen die Ukraine. Die wichtigsten Neuigkeiten im Überblick.

nzz.title: KURZMELDUNGEN - Wirtschaft: Stefan Hartung tritt als Bosch-Chef ab +++ Ex-CEO geht laut Medienbericht nach Kündigung gegen Nestlé vor
Das Erdbeben in Venezuela wird zum Stresstest für das Regime in Caracas
nzz.description: Naturkatastrophen können in Lateinamerika politisch explosiv sein – vor allem für autoritäre Regime. Erdbeben haben bereits politische Dynastien zerstört, aber auch politische Karrieren beflügelt.

observador.title: Picas: "Não há distinção entre a minha música e o meu nome"
observador.description: Picas apresenta o disco de estreia "Vendavais", onde explora temas autobiográficos e provocadores. A cantora prepara um espetáculo especial para o dia 10 de julho no NOS Alive.

observador.title: Serviços essenciais têm nova estratégia para lidar com crise
observador.description: Dois novos instrumentos avaliam risco e elaboram de planos de resiliência para setores como energia, saúde, água e transportes, em caso de terrorismo, alterações climáticas ou cibercriminalidade.

observador.title: Nova reforma laboral. "Quanto mais depressa melhor"
observador.description: Palma Ramalho diz que Governo deve voltar à reforma laboral o mais depressa possível. Desvaloriza impopularidade e reitera ter missão a cumprir. Não exclui salário mínimo acima dos 970 euros em 2027.

observador.title: Portugal com níveis elevados de pólen na atmosfera
observador.description: Oliveira, castanheiro, gramíneas e urticáceas dominam a polinização até 2 de julho. Algarve e ilhas ficam a salvo, com níveis baixos previstos.

observador.title: Grávida dá à luz entre os escombros após sismos
observador.description: Com a mulher iluminada pelas lanternas dos telefones que a rodeavam entre os escombros de um prédio que ruiu, um grupo de cidadãos contribuiu para um parto improvisado com sucesso.

observador.title: Governo reforça fiscalização da canábis medicinal
observador.description: Revisão do decreto-lei da canábis medicinal e reforço do Infarmed estão entre as respostas anunciadas após acusação de 24 arguidos ligados ao setor.

observador.title: UE elogia forma como Portugal protegeu liberdade após adesão
observador.description: Roberta Metsola discursou no Mosteiro dos Jerónimos, para comemorar o 40.º aniversário da adesão portuguesa à UE. Paulo Rangel destacou que Portugal quer "melhorar a abertura da Europa ao mundo".

observador.title: PJ: cocaína apreendida daria para 410 milhões de doses
observador.description: Entre 2025 e maio de 2026, as autoridades portuguesas apreenderam cocaína suficiente para 410 milhões de doses. Mais de 6.200 pessoas foram detidas por tráfico.

observador.title: Madeira envia 18 operacionais para a Venezuela
observador.description: Equipa multidisciplinar integra bombeiros, proteção civil e um médico. Missão está estimada em 12 dias, mas data de partida ainda não foi anunciada.

observador.title: Cinemateca dedica ciclo a Bruce Springsteen
observador.description: De "Filadélfia" a "Jerry Maguire", passando pelo recente "Deliver me from nowhere" (2025), a Cinemateca Portuguesa exibe a partir de 1 de julho os filmes que moldaram o "Boss".

observador.title: Associação alerta para escassez de médicos do trabalho
observador.description: A APEMT diz que a escassez de médicos do trabalho coloca "milhares de empresas" em insegurança jurídica e pede medidas extraordinárias ao Governo.

observador.title: Ténis. Nuno Borges afastado do torneio de Maiorca
observador.description: O tenista português perdeu por 6-1 e 6-2 com o norte-americano Ethan Quinn. Em Wimbledon, estreia-se frente a Tristan Boyer, vindo da qualificação.

observador.title: Ataques rebeldes deslocam 52 mil crianças em 6 meses
observador.description: Desde janeiro, 52 mil crianças foram deslocadas por ataques rebeldes no norte de Moçambique. O conflito, com 6.632 mortos desde 2017, alastra a novas áreas.

observador.title: Mação ainda sem telecomunicações cinco meses após Kristin
observador.description: O presidente da câmara fala em "vergonha" e aponta falhas de operadoras e da IP. Prejuízos no concelho chegam aos 6 milhões de euros.

observador.title: Polícia investiga anúncios na Vinted por suspeita de tráfico
observador.description: Anúncios atribuem preços exorbitantes ou medidas humanas a peluches e brinquedos. Imagens começaram por ser partilhadas como suspeitas nas redes sociais, mas autoridades já estão a investigar.

observador.title: RTP: aumento de 57 euros após greve
observador.description: O STT e a administração da RTP chegaram a acordo. Os 57 euros de aumento salarial têm efeitos retroativos a janeiro de 2026, com pagamento em julho.

observador.title: PJ detém homem de 24 anos em Lisboa por abuso de menor
observador.description: Crimes terão ocorrido quando a criança, atualmente com 13 anos, tinha entre 4 e 8 anos, altura em que "o suspeito tinha acesso facilitado ao menor", dado que a sua mãe era cuidadora informal.

observador.title: 16h. INEM investiga morte de jovem devido a falha no socorro
observador.description: O INEM está a investigar o caso da morte de uma jovem de 20 anos em Vila Real relacionada com uma falha na prestação de socorro. Ainda neste jornal, a atualização do número de mortes na Venezuela.

spiegel.title: WM 2026 News heute: Bastian Schweinsteiger wehrt sich gegen Rassismusvorwurf
spiegel.description: ARD-Experte Bastian Schweinsteiger sieht in seinen Äußerungen über »den afrikanischen Fußball« kein Problem. Und: zwischen den Spielern Uruguays und ihrem Trainer Marcelo Bielsa gibt es Zoff. Die WM-News des Tages.

spiegel.title: Halle (Saale): Neue Züge der S-Bahn zu lang für mehrere Bahnsteige
spiegel.description: Kein Ausstieg aus diesem Zugteil: Den neuen, langen S-Bahnen auf der Strecke zwischen Leipzig und Halle geht an einigen Haltestellen der Bahnsteig aus. Der Betreiber verspricht Besserung – bis Ende 2028.

spiegel.title: Hitze: 40,9 Grad – Wetterdienst meldet Juni-Hitzerekord
spiegel.description: Erstmals seit Beginn der Aufzeichnungen wurden im Juni mehr als 40 Grad in Deutschland gemessen. Die Marke könnte am Wochenende vielerorts überschritten werden. Und: Großveranstaltungen werden in ganz Europa abgesagt. Das News-Update.

spiegel.title: Bremen: Zwei getötete Menschen gefunden – Täter auf der Flucht
spiegel.description: Ein Mann und eine Frau wurden mit tödlichen Verletzungen aufgefunden. Die Polizei Bremen fahndet nun nach einer unbekannten Person.

spiegel.title: Nazi-Verfolgung: Zeugen Jehovas erzielen Etappensieg im Streit über Familienarchiv
spiegel.description: Ein Archiv erzählt von der Verfolgung der Zeugen Jehovas durch die Nazis. Derzeit liegt es in einem Museum, die Sekte erhebt aber Anspruch darauf. Jetzt wurde ihre Position durch ein Urteil gestärkt.

spiegel.title: Iran - Anschlagspläne auf Volker Beck: Prozess gegen mutmaßliche Agenten gestartet
spiegel.description: Im Auftrag Irans sollen zwei Männer Juden und Freunde Israels in Deutschland für Anschläge ausgespäht haben. Zum Prozessauftakt warnt der Bundesanwalt vor einer Ausweitung terroristischer Angriffe durch die Revolutionswächter.

spiegel.title: Volkswagen: Kann VW wirklich 100.000 Jobs streichen? Vier Szenarien
spiegel.description: Der größte deutsche Autobauer will offenbar doppelt so viele Stellen abbauen wie bislang vereinbart. Das geht nur auf eine Weise: Sparen, bis es quietscht. Selbst bestehende Jobgarantien stehen offenbar auf dem Prüfstand.

spiegel.title: Sergej Iwanow: Ehemaliger Verteidigungsminister von Russland ist tot
spiegel.description: Er galt einst als einer der engsten Vertrauten Putins sowie als sein möglicher Nachfolger: Russlands früherer Verteidigungsminister Sergej Iwanow ist im Alter von 73 Jahren gestorben.

spiegel.title: Riesen-Planeten TOI-791 b und TOI-791 c sind fluffiger als Zuckerwatte
spiegel.description: Sie sind groß wie Jupiter, wiegen aber nur einen Bruchteil davon: Astronomen haben zwei Riesenplaneten von extrem geringer Dichte entdeckt. Die Forscher sprechen von »Super-Puffs«.

spiegel.title: Neues Album »Harmony« von Brutalismus 3000: Parolen wie Projektile
spiegel.description: Professionalisierte Hymnen für den kommenden Aufstand: Auf »Harmony« zeigt sich das gefeierte Berliner Techno-Duo Brutalismus 3000 als subversives, antikapitalistisches Mobilisierungskommando.

spiegel.title: Fußball-WM heute: Das sollten Sie vor den Spielen am Abend und in der Nacht wissen
spiegel.description: Duell der Superstars in Boston, Kap Verdes Traum von der K.-o.-Runde und Belgiens Zitterpartie: Der letzte Spieltag in den Gruppen G, H und I verspricht Spannung. Das müssen Sie wissen.

spiegel.title: Porsche Taycan mit e-Shift im Test: Elektroauto mit Fake-Getriebe
spiegel.description: Porsche rüstet sein Elektromodell Taycan mit einer virtuellen Gangschaltung aus, um Benziner zu spielen. Alberner Quatsch? Eine Testfahrt zeigt: Das Fake-Getriebe bringt Fahrspaß – und sogar etwas Sinn.

spiegel.title: Erdbeben in Venezuela: »Eine Größenordnung von 20.000 bis 30.000 Toten ist leider realistisch«
spiegel.description: Der Boden »verflüssigte« sich, Gebäude kippten wie sinkende Schiffe: Der Bauingenieur Božidar Stojadinović erklärt, warum das Erdbeben in Venezuela so verheerende Folgen hat – und warum das Schlimmste womöglich noch bevorsteht.

spiegel.title: Dieter Nuhr will Witze über Gewalt an Frauen nicht so gemeint haben
spiegel.description: In seiner Sendung »Nuhr im Ersten« riet Dieter Nuhr Frauen, zum Schutz vor Gewalt einen Partner vor dem Sex »einfach erst mal kennenzulernen«. Auf die laute Kritik antwortet der Komiker nun mit einem Erklärungsversuch.

spiegel.title: Ketamin: Deutschland ist zweitgrößter Umschlagplatz in Europa
spiegel.description: Deutschland ist einem Uno-Bericht zufolge einer der wichtigsten Drehscheiben für den illegalen Handel mit Ketamin in Europa. Nur die Niederlande spielen eine größere Rolle.

spiegel.title: Magdeburg – Urteil nach Anschlag: »Er hatte die Absicht, alle, die ihm in den Weg kamen, zu töten«
spiegel.description: Das Landgericht Magdeburg verurteilt den Todesfahrer vom Weihnachtsmarkt zur höchsten Strafe, die das deutsche Strafrecht kennt. Politik und Justiz könnte der Fall aber noch weiter beschäftigen.

spiegel.title: Bosch: Stefan Hartung hört überraschend als Vorsitzender der Geschäftsführung auf
spiegel.description: Gerade noch den Vertrag verlängert, jetzt ist plötzlich Schluss: Stefan Hartung hört als Vorsitzender der Geschäftsführung von Bosch auf. Sein Nachfolger an der Spitze des Technologiekonzerns steht bereits fest.

spiegel.title: Deutsche Bahn: Switch-Tausch – ausbleibende Fehlermeldung sorgte für Chaos
spiegel.description: Alle Züge standen still, weil die DB-IT nicht mehr wollte: Die Bahn hat die Ursache für den bundesweiten Zugstillstand mitgeteilt. Damit das nicht noch mal vorkommt, will sie die Technik künftig erst nach Mitternacht warten.

letemps.title: La star du curling suisse Alina Pätz rejoint le CC Genève avec sa nouvelle équipe et vise l’or olympique
letemps.description:
Déjà fort de sa «dream team» masculine, le Curling Club Trois-Chêne annonce ce vendredi l’arrivée de l’équipe d’élite féminine menée par la vice-championne olympique, dans le cadre d’un vaste projet de développement de la relève

Le centre de gravité du curling suisse penche décidément du côté de Genève. Déjà fort de la «dream team» masculine du skip Yannick Schwaller, le Curling Club Trois-Ch

new-sci.description: This August a total solar eclipse is set to be visible across parts of Europe, while a partial eclipse will sweep across about a quarter of the planet – here’s how to catch it

new-sci.title: If you aren't terrified by this heatwave, you should be
new-sci.description: The extreme heat currently being felt in Europe isn’t the new normal – much worse is to come, and we are doing far too little to adapt, says Michael Le Page

new-sci.description: IBM's latest chip packs in twice as many transistors as the current state-of-the-art chip by adding a second layer of silicon circuitry

new-sci.title: Possible signs of ancient life on Mars are rich in complex carbon
new-sci.description: An instrument on the Perseverance rover has identified large, complex carbon compounds alongside unusual patterns on the surface of rocks that resemble traces of microbial activity

phys-org.title: Global rice paddy greenhouse gas emissions have doubled during the past six decades, study shows
phys-org.description: Rice paddy greenhouse gas emissions have doubled during the past 60 years—but practical farm changes could cut methane emissions and support global climate targets without reducing food production, a team led by Boston College scientists reports in the journal Nature Food.

phys-org.title: Floods kill two in Taiwan as twin storms approach Japan
phys-org.description: Japan advised more than a million people to leave their homes as two tropical storms swept toward the archipelago Friday, with torrential rain also pounding Taiwan, where at least two people have been killed.

phys-org.title: European heatwave's unlikely accomplice: An ocean 'cold blob'
phys-org.description: The heat wave battering Europe may have an unlikely partner in crime: a patch of cold ocean water south of Iceland and Greenland that can influence weather patterns over the continent.

phys-org.title: Whitebait rapidly switch life cycles when earthquakes cut off route to sea
phys-org.description: Aotearoa New Zealand whitebait can rapidly switch their life cycles in response to sudden environmental changes, new University of Otago—Ōtākou Whakaihu Waka research shows. The research is published in the journal Nature Communications.

phys-org.title: Moderate harmful algal bloom predicted for western Lake Erie. Could impact coastal recreation by mid-July
phys-org.description: NOAA and its research partners are forecasting a moderate harmful algal bloom (HAB) in western Lake Erie this summer. This year's bloom is expected to measure 3.5 on the HAB severity index, with a potential range of 3 to 4.5. Experts from NOAA and their government and academic partners discussed the 2026 Seasonal Forecast of Harmful Algal Blooms for Lake Erie during a free public webinar on June 25 hosted by Ohio Sea Grant and Stone Laboratory.

phys-org.title: Europe heat wave shattering temperature records
phys-org.description: Europe's heat wave has smashed several temperature records, the U.N.'s weather and climate agency said Friday, adding that it would determine the full impact once the phenomenon has ended.

phys-org.title: Elusive thorium–thorium bonding directly observed using Hirshfeld atom refinement
phys-org.description: Researchers have directly visualized a rare type of chemical bond between some of the heaviest elements in the periodic table, providing experimental evidence of how these atoms share electrons in systems where this has been difficult to prove.

phys-org.title: Genomics study reveals how endangered island oaks exhibit contrasting evolutionary paths
phys-org.description: Researchers have conducted a conservation genomics study on two critically endangered island oaks—Quercus bawanglingensis and Quercus pseudosetulosa. They assembled high-quality chromosome-level genomes and revealed how natural selection and demographic history have shaped their markedly different genomic architectures. The study, led by Prof. Wang Baosheng at the South China Botanical Garden (SCBG) of the Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS), was recently published in The Plant Journal.

phys-org.title: Marine heat waves pose significant threat to seagrass restoration efforts
phys-org.description: A marine heat wave has undermined the success of seagrass restoration efforts at a site in north Wales, new research has found. More than 1.1 million seagrass seeds were planted at sites in two bays in north Wales between 2023 and 2024 as part of Seagrass Ocean Rescue: North Wales, the U.K.'s largest active seagrass restoration program. Despite being located less than 50 kilometers (31 miles) apart, the planting efforts in Bae Caergybi saw seedling establishment and overwinter survival, whi

phys-org.title: Ancient ocean circulation reversed Atlantic and Pacific oxygen patterns 15 million years ago
phys-org.description: The eastern tropical Pacific Ocean is known for its large low-oxygen zones that are increasing in size, putting marine life at risk. New research shows that 15 million years ago, the opposite was true.

phys-org.title: Swiss glaciers have exhausted their snow reserves
phys-org.description: From June 29 onward, Switzerland's glaciers will have exhausted their snow reserves. Every liter of meltwater now causes them to lose mass—this is Glacier Loss Day. Between the extreme years of 2003 and 2022 alone, 200 square kilometers of ice—an area almost as large as the canton of Zug—have disappeared. This is reflected in the volume of meltwater, as analyses show: Although ice loss was more severe in the summer of 2022 than in 2003, less water flowed off the glaciers.

phys-org.title: Do animal behavior experiments give a distorted view of cooperation?
phys-org.description: When biologists study cooperation in animals, they usually offer just a single task at a time. But what happens when animals can choose among several opportunities to work together? Biologists at Utrecht University discovered that this can make a remarkable difference.

phys-org.title: Grade inflation in pandemic strengthened university prospects for private school and disadvantaged students
phys-org.description: The first empirical evidence of how A-level grading in the pandemic affected university applications corroborates concerns about disproportionate benefits for private schools. Disadvantaged students also benefited, however, and the long-term effects for these groups could provide valuable information about how to close the university admissions gap.

phys-org.title: Secrets of how we see color revealed at the molecular level
phys-org.description: A global team has cracked a decades-old mystery, revealing the atomic structures of the molecules in our eyes that allow us to see colors. "To understand how we detect light and perceive colors, we need to know the exact structure of light-sensitive molecules in our eyes," said The Australian National University (ANU) researcher Emeritus Professor Trevor Lamb.

phys-org.title: Want to be a better reader? Here's how to practice active reading
phys-org.description: If you're part of Gen Z, chances are you rely on social media for news and current events. And if you're under 30, you're more likely to trust what you see on social media than any other age cohort, according to Pew Research Center data.

phys-org.title: Tiny raptor, tiny range: GPS tracking reveals pygmy falcons use less than 1 km² to raise nestlings
phys-org.description: A new study, published in the Journal of Raptor Research, reveals that Africa's smallest diurnal bird of prey, the pygmy falcon (Polihierax semitorquatus), operates within one of the smallest breeding home ranges ever recorded for a raptor.

phys-org.title: When a pool or pond turns green with algae, don't reach for chemicals—nature has better solutions
phys-org.description: When the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool turned green with algae just days after a US$15 million renovation, the U.S. government scrambled for chemicals and expensive technical solutions to fix the iconic landmark.

phys-org.title: A single origin story for the Milky Way's most mysterious stars
phys-org.description: Lurking at the heart of the Milky Way, Sagittarius A* (Sgr A*) is a supermassive black hole four million times the mass of the sun, surrounded by a puzzling collection of young, massive stars whose orbits have long defied explanation. Astronomers have proposed various competing theories to account for these stars, but none has been able to explain all of them together.

undark.title: The MAHA Movement’s Worrisome Embrace of Ibogaine
undark.description: The MAHA movement has been promoting the plant-based substance ibogaine as a remedy for opioid addiction, despite the lack of clinical trials on its safety and efficacy. One physician who practices addiction medicine discusses the risks of ibogaine and argues for the need to support proven treatments.

undark.title: Advocacy Groups Express Mixed Views on Embryo Editing
undark.description: At least two new start-up companies, Preventive and Origin Genomics, say they are developing strategies that combine gene editing with in vitro fertilization to correct disease-causing mutations. Advocacy groups for people living with these genetic disorders have been quiet on the developments.

undark.title: Interview: California Lawmaker Calls for a Peptide Working Group
undark.description: Amid a national push to ease restrictions on certain peptides, California legislator Joe Patterson has introduced a state-level bill that would to establish a working group tasked with making recommendations to allow physicians and hospitals, among others, to prescribe and study promising peptides.

undark.title: Making Sense of Data From Wearable Health Trackers
undark.description: Wearable health devices such as smartwatches, glucose monitors, and sleep trackers are blurring the line between consumer wellness and clinical medicine. One physician argues that validation standards and privacy protections must be established to ensure the usefulness of the data these devices generate.

undark.title: In California, a Plan to Help Wildlife Cross a Busy Freeway
undark.description: The 101 freeway in California bisects a mountainous region where threatened cougars and other animals are blocked without a viable path across 10 lanes of heavily trafficked roadway. But an ambitious 210-foot “vegetated bridge” will soon be home to what organizers say is the largest wildlife crossing anywhere in the world.

undark.title: Promising ‘Liquid Biopsies’ May Not Be Ready for Primetime
undark.description: Multi-cancer early detection tests seek to spot cancer from a single blood draw. Enabling earlier cancer diagnoses could help save lives and limit the need for invasive interventions. But while the tests are promising, physicians have expressed doubt about routine use by low-risk and asymptomatic individuals.

undark.title: Book Review: How Radio Astronomy Made the Invisible Visible
undark.description: According to astronomer Emma Chapman’s revelatory “The Echoing Universe,” the history of radio astronomy is filled with surprises that have revealed parts of the universe that would otherwise remain hidden and invisible — DIY instruments, secrets accidentally uncovered, and persistent connections to Earth.

undark.title: Risk Aversion in Science Stifles Innovation
undark.description: Does the scientific enterprise play it too safe? C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that risk-taking in science involves a willingness to reflect on the processes and incentives of the profession — and to dramatically overhaul them if they do not work. Only then can true scientific innovation take shape.

undark.title: A Peptide, a Secretive Scientist, and a Debate Over Evidence
undark.description: Access to unapproved peptides like BPC-157 has become a cause célèbre for the MAHA movement. Undark contributing editor Sara Talpos digs into the untold history of BPC-157 and its long journey from the scientific margins to the center of a debate over U.S. drug regulation.

undark.title: Book Review: Within Our Cells, the Miracle of Constant Mutation
undark.description: Our cells are constantly mutating in a battle for the survival of the fittest that is raging inside us daily, Roxanne Khamsi writes in “Beyond Inheritance.” Many of these mutations are harmless, others are cellular deviants that lead to disease, and remarkably, some can actually self-correct.

proj-syn.title: Is a European Single Market for Energy Such a Good Idea?
proj-syn.description: Although textbook microeconomics shows why less energy-market fragmentation would be better for Europe as a whole, that does not mean it would be a good deal for countries producing low-carbon electricity at minimal marginal cost. In fact, if more integration creates free riders, the political backlash could be profound.

proj-syn.title: China’s Failed Rebalancing
proj-syn.description: When China’s leaders first acknowledged the need to rebalance the economy nearly two decades ago, it seemed like a matter of when, not if. But with the household consumption share of Chinese GDP remaining stubbornly low, officials’ promises to boost domestic demand have lost all credibility.

proj-syn.title: Crowning a Healthy Populism
proj-syn.description: Although recent political mobilizations in Hungary, Albania, and other parts of Central and Eastern Europe could be described as populist and nationalist, they have little in common with the aggressive ethnonationalism that MAGA professes. Could they be a model for a new form of politics?

proj-syn.title: Why Rules-Based Orders Fail
proj-syn.description: For a brief period after the Cold War, Americans persuaded themselves that the liberal order had become self-sustaining. And yet, any rules-based system elaborate enough to govern and interpret its own operations will eventually confront questions that its rules cannot answer.

proj-syn.title: The Tide Is Turning Against Russia
proj-syn.description: With Ukraine reclaiming territory, mounting drone strikes deep in Russian territory, and draining Russia’s coffers, Vladimir Putin would do well to seek a negotiated freeze to the conflict. But there is no guarantee that he will, not least because he might not grasp the situation Russia is in.

proj-syn.title: Managing Sino-American Interdependence
proj-syn.description: At their summit last month, US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping seemed to recognize that they are in the same boat. If either the United States or China tries to cripple or decouple from the other, it will harm its own firms, consumers, financial markets, and innovation ecosystem.

proj-syn.title: Who Gains in an AI-Supercharged Economy?
proj-syn.description: If AI delivers as promised and fundamentally transforms the economy, we will have moved from the current investment phase, where AI builders dominate, to one where AI users will reap the greatest reward. That is what happens every time an innovation becomes a general-purpose technology.

proj-syn.title: Development in a Time of Disruption
proj-syn.description: Once firms and economies ascend to market dominance, they often kick away the ladder behind them and erect barriers to market entry to stymie would-be challengers. But developing countries can and do leapfrog incumbent technologies, and conditions for doing so may be particularly favorable now.

proj-syn.title: Trump’s Un-American Capitalism
proj-syn.description: The current US administration's openly corrupt style of crony capitalism is the antithesis of the institutional foundation on which the US economy was built. The winners in the new oligarchic competition are not those who make the best products, but rather those who are best at flattering the mad king.

proj-syn.title: Can the Manchester Model Save Britain?
proj-syn.description: Following a decades-long effort to lay the foundations for economic dynamism, Greater Manchester has become the UK’s fastest-growing region. While the Manchester model cannot be precisely replicated at the national level, it does carry important lessons for outgoing Prime Minister Keir Starmer's likely successor.

proj-syn.title: How Trillionaires Are Really Made
proj-syn.description: Some may argue that the world’s first trillionaire is a story of technological triumph and a win for American capitalism. But markets have not bet on cutting-edge technology or a company too big to fail, but rather on the idea of a mega-monopolist with wealth and influence so vast that the US government will not allow him to fail.

proj-syn.title: Cities Show How Climate Action Makes Life Better
proj-syn.description: Cities have shown that a combination of adaptation measures and energy efficiency can save lives, improve well-being, reduce energy costs, and create conditions for sustainable growth. A new partnership seeks to help mayors and city leaders scale up these efforts through technical and financial assistance.

proj-syn.title: The Myth of Global Chaos
proj-syn.description: Today’s seemingly nonstop international tumult is not as unintelligible as it seems. What pundits lazily describe as chaos is the culmination of developments that were long in the making and arrived at a time when the international system was no longer able to prevent or mitigate geopolitical shocks.

proj-syn.title: The Microfinance Debate Is Missing the Point
proj-syn.description: For too long, policymakers, economists, and investors have focused on whether microfinance actually helps people, reducing a complex issue to a meaningless yes-or-no verdict. The most important questions concern how loans are designed, delivered, and regulated, who receives them, and what they are used for.

proj-syn.title: Turning Latin America’s Resilience Into Growth
proj-syn.description: Economic stabilization has been a significant achievement for Latin America and the Caribbean, a region with a long history of financial crises. But these countries need a well-sequenced reform agenda to attract private investment and create the growth engine that will translate hard-won gains into higher living standards.

proj-syn.title: The World Cup vs. the Extremists
proj-syn.description: Germany’s 2026 World Cup team, like so many others in the tournament, shows that loving one’s country and welcoming newcomers are not incompatible impulses. Although activists on the far left and the far right would have us believe otherwise, most ordinary people implicitly recognize this.

proj-syn.title: Beyond Brexit—and Back to Europe
proj-syn.description: Those who follow only intergovernmental negotiations or debates in the media might think that nothing has changed in the decade since the United Kingdom's voters decided to leave the European Union. Yet new polling finds that large majorities on both sides of the English Channel now support re-engagement.

proj-syn.title: Trump’s March of Folly in Iran
proj-syn.description: In promoting his “deal” with Iran, US President Donald Trump has tried to dress up a humiliating defeat as a victory. While it’s tempting to blame this outcome on incompetent leadership, it stems more from the policies and institutions that have allowed entertainers and profiteers to rise to power.
